title: Reverse a LinkedList [Iterative]
stepTitle: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
category: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
problemStatement: Reverse a singly linked list iteratively.
intuition: Walk the list flipping one next pointer at a time. You need three references: the node before, the current node, and the next node you are about to lose.

approaches.title: Optimal: prev / curr / next
approaches.idea: Save next, flip, advance both pointers.
approaches.code:
def reverse_list(head):
    prev = None
    curr = head
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    return prev
approaches.dryRun:
1->2->3
curr=1: 1->None, prev=1
curr=2: 2->1, prev=2
curr=3: 3->2, prev=3 -> head 3
approaches.whyWorks: Each iteration reverses exactly one edge while preserving access to the untouched suffix.

edgeCases: Losing the head reference in the caller
commonMistakes: Not saving curr.next before overwriting it
patternRecognition: Pointer rewiring: reverse in k-groups, palindrome check, reorder list
followUps: Reverse a sublist between positions m and n
interviewInsight: Draw the three pointers before coding. Interviewers can tell instantly whether you understand or memorised it.
